location.anchor: Unnumbered functional immediately following equation (9.5), and p=0 parenthetical

issues.source_claim: h^(1-p) S_K=c dtheta is the Euler-Lagrange equation for F_p=(1/p) integral h^p +(1/c)|K|.

assumptions.verification: Smooth strictly convex origin-symmetric compact body, h=1>0, S=dtheta, p>=-n; K_t=(1+t)B^3 for |t|<1/2 is an admissible symmetric support perturbation.

issues.complete_check: F_2(K_t)=2*pi*(1+t)^2+(4*pi/3)*(1+t)^3; derivative at t=0 is 8*pi, not the asserted zero. General derivative on solutions is 2*integral q*h^(p-1), positive for q=1.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: A sign change plausibly expresses the intended formula; it is not the displayed formula.
No volume constraint stated; adding one changes the variational assertion.
Main Section 6 functional has the correct different signs and does not depend on this application.
arXiv2408.08171v4 HTML retains the two plus signs; only this focused comparison was made.
issues.impact: Invalidates the local Euler-Lagrange characterization and the variational justification of the auxiliary application as written. No demonstrated damage to Theorem 1.1.

repair.statement: Use -1/p integral h^p + |K|/c, or -integral log h + |K|/c for p=0.
repair.verification: Analytic first variation gives exactly -h^(p-1)dtheta+S_K/c, with even test functions sufficient for even measures.
repair.limits: Verified for smooth origin-symmetric bodies with positive support and curvature; does not independently prove full nonsmooth uniqueness or equality claims.
